title: AutoTestRunner suite
description: How to start and reset an app, and the suite's variables.

startWindow.description: The title of the window it opens first, when that isn't its main window, such as a sign-in window. A useWindow step moves on to the main window.

runAsAdmin.description: Restarts autotest as administrator, as the app needs it.

status.description: An element whose text says what the app is doing, such as a status bar. Its text before each click is kept for waitText's new.

firstExisting.description: The first path that exists, relative to the suite folder; the last when none does.

regex.description: ${name(value)} gives the regex's first group in value.

requires.description: Paths that must exist before a run starts. If one doesn't, autotest exits with code 2.

script.description: A .ps1 or .cs file that removes what the suite leaves on the machine. A .cs runs with dotnet run, which needs the .NET 10 SDK.

leftovers.description: A .ps1 or .cs file that prints one line for each thing an earlier run left; nothing on a clean machine.

databases.description: Databases that query steps and dbValue checks use, by a name of your own.

kind.description: sqlServer for SQL Server, Express and LocalDB; mySql for MySQL and MariaDB.

connection.description: Its connection string, as its .NET driver takes it; ${variables} allowed, so a password can come from --var.

queues.description: Message queues that send, receive and purge steps and queue checks use, by a name of your own.

queue.description: The queue's name, or for MSMQ its path, such as .\private$\orders.

connection.description: The broker: amqp://user:password@host:5672/ for RabbitMQ, host(port) for IBM MQ.

channel.description: IBM MQ's server connection channel, such as DEV.APP.SVRCONN.

queueManager.description: IBM MQ's queue manager, such as QM1.

user.description: IBM MQ's user, when the channel asks for one.

format.description: How an MSMQ message's text is written: xml, as .NET's XmlMessageFormatter does (the default), or plain text.

screen.description: The smallest screen the suite is written for.

builder.description: What the builder does while recording a case.

watch.description: Controls whose text the builder watches: when it changes after a step, it adds a wait for the new text. The app's status, and any element with a macro named waitFor and its name, are watched anyway.

element.description: The control, by its name in elements.json.

call.description: The macro that waits for it, given startsWith when it takes it. A waitText when left out.

check.description: Also keeps what it said, and checks it at the checkpoint.

afterClick.description: Steps the builder adds after a control is clicked, instead of a wait for the status text.

element.description: The control clicked, by its name in elements.json.

call.description: The macro to run after it.

delay.description: Seconds to wait before the macro, as a wait step.
